\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آمپول} (âmpul)}{آمپول (âmpul)}]{\fa{آمپول} (âmpul) — an injection}

\label{lesson:FA-C189-ampul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to swing, then the Persian for to install.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آمپول}}
\textbf{\fa{آمپول}} — \emph{âmpul} — \textquotedblleft{}an injection\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âmpul} is borrowed from French \emph{ampoule}, \textquotedblleft{}phial\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). The French word goes back to Latin \emph{ampulla}, \textquotedblleft{}small flask\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\label{lesson:FA-C189-noskhe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to install, then the Persian for an injection.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نسخه}}
\textbf{\fa{نسخه}} — \emph{noskhe} — \textquotedblleft{}a prescription\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{noskhe} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{nusḫa}, \textquotedblleft{}copy\textquotedblright{}. Its Arabic root is \emph{n-s-ḫ} (Lane). Persian also uses it for a prescription.
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{\fa{آزمایش}} — \emph{âzmâyesh} — \textquotedblleft{}a medical test\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{âzmâyesh} is \emph{âzmâ-}, the present stem of \emph{âzmudan}, \textquotedblleft{}to test\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-yesh}: a test. The verb is native, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{uzmūdan}.
